title: Home Sessions V2
author: Duncan
desc: An asynchronous, irregular split designed for my summer in VA. Training is every single day but can easily be variable if more rest is needed or something like travel comes up. I find higher frequencies with lower volumes allow me to recover while still pushing each set as hard as possible without fatiguing within a workout. All the movements are pretty simple, yet effective. This isn't a difficult program to follow because it's pretty much 0-1 RIR on everything, however it's a lot of training for a beginner. I am also doing this from my home gym, so it doesn't matter that I'm only doing relatively little volume per session. If you're thinking of running this in a commercial gym but have to commute, it might just not be worth it.

ss.note: Full scapular protraction at the top
I will always perform on these days, but I may just throw in extra volume if abs are recovered
Trap focus. Keep raising hips to get more reps until the weight won't move
2nd highest bench setting with knees on the bench. Raise hands as high as they can go
Full scapular protraction at the top
trap focused. Start parallel but perform a mechanical drop set by raising the torso

ex.note: Lat focused. Arch back and lean into the working side to better connect with the lat. Put knee on bench to standardize the movement. Can move to tripod stance once I get stronger

ss.note: ATG style. Take a huge step back and get a massive hip-flexor stretch
Thumbless for extra forearm work
go in between a doorway and hold on to both sides for support
Hamstring focus. Completely locked out knees
Keep hands pronated as I raise overhead
Glute focus. Slight knee bend but minimize knee extension

ex.note: Keep back flat on the bench while reaching as far across the body as possible
